recommended_install.command: npx -y --prefer-online socraticode@latest (upstream MCP-server launcher, launched by the host); for a reproducible candidate use socraticode@1.15.0 in the same launcher. Upstream requires Node.js 18.17+ with npx and, for its default Qdrant/Ollama setup, Docker; an externally configured service profile is also supported.

claude_code.how: MCP-only: claude mcp add --scope user socraticode -- npx -y --prefer-online socraticode@latest. Plugin alternative: claude plugin marketplace add giancarloerra/socraticode, then claude plugin install --scope user socraticode@socraticode; open a new session and index, check status, then search. Use one registration route. The plugin adds exploration/management skills and an explorer agent; v1.15.0 allows its engine to be pinned with SOCRATICODE_SPEC=socraticode@1.15.0, while its default still floats.

codex.how: MCP-only: codex mcp add socraticode -- npx -y --prefer-online socraticode@latest. Plugin alternative: codex plugin marketplace add giancarloerra/socraticode --ref main, then codex plugin add socraticode@socraticode; start a new task. The Codex plugin uses the shared .mcp.json launcher, which still specifies socraticode@latest; SOCRATICODE_SPEC is a Claude-plugin feature, so pin a standalone Codex launcher explicitly when reproducibility is required.

official_baseline_claims.claim: Upstream advertises 61% less context, 84% fewer tool calls and 37x faster exploration than grep-based exploration in its VS Code benchmark, using Claude Opus 4.6 on a 2.45-million-line codebase. These are upstream task/benchmark claims, not a 1.14.0-to-1.15.0 comparison, our stack's results, or provider-billing savings.

Search combines dense semantic retrieval and BM25 with reciprocal-rank fusion, and the default auto watcher refreshes an indexed project. The server also exposes dependency/symbol graphs and searchable context artifacts; these are retrieval capabilities rather than a native token-savings counter.

limitations.text: Indexing is asynchronous; check codebase_status and search after indexing completes. codebase_status reports index progress/state and chunk counts, not saved tokens; search results still need checking against the original source.

Coverage depends on indexing scope and ignore rules. Dot-files and dot-directories are excluded by default, so a search miss is not evidence that a hidden configuration or agent definition does not exist.

Watcher/manual/off settings determine freshness: disabling the watcher and startup recovery deliberately leaves a snapshot requiring explicit codebase_update. Branch indexes are shared by default; branch-aware indexing is opt-in and an explicit project ID overrides branch separation.

Embedding and vector-storage services are prerequisites, not provided by a bare MCP registration. The default uses local Ollama and Qdrant; alternate endpoints require compatible embedding dimensions/model configuration. This does not route Claude/Codex generation traffic or prove prompt-cache savings.

The Claude plugin's duplicate-registration notice is a SessionStart hook; it does not intercept arbitrary reads or compress every tool result. MCP-only adoption does not automatically install the plugin's agent/skill instructions.

new_since_pin.text: v1.15.0 adds SOCRATICODE_SPEC expansion to .claude-plugin/mcp.json so the Claude plugin's engine can be pinned. The shared .mcp.json used by Codex/Cursor remains unchanged and floating.
v1.15.0 waits for collection creation already in progress in the same process before reading it, addressing the initial-index/status Qdrant race tracked in issue #176.
v1.15.0 retains the underlying Qdrant error reason and delivers MCP logging notifications, addressing issue #178; clients must tolerate the new notifications/message stream.

v1.15.0 expands and corrects PHP graph extraction/resolution, including scoped aliases, qualified/static calls, inheritance, typed properties, structural/type edges and non-ASCII identifiers, while reducing repeated parser traversal. The release does not claim a new measured model-token reduction.

The pins file now drives bootstrap installation, superseding the older decision text that said no pin entry existed. native_adaptation.claude_wiring: Standalone stdio MCP scoped to the main project: live $HOME/.claude.json stores the socraticode entry under projects for $HOME/code/native-agent-stack, with no user-global socraticode entry; technically this is private project/local configuration, not a committed .mcp.json registration. The portable server definition is examples/claude-mcp.json.example; adoption/templates/claude.settings.template.json contains no socraticode MCP registration. It launches the pinned 1.14.0 dist/index.js with external Qdrant and the lmstudio-compatible embedding adapter. examples/claude-native/agents/isolated-builder.md and evidence-reviewer.md explicitly allow SocratiCode tools and direct conceptual-code retrieval; those definitions still require an available server in their actual project.
native_adaptation.codex_wiring: Codex USER scope, moved by docs/decisions/2026-09-25-codex-mcp-scope.md, Decision 1, and documented in docs/token-session-handbook.md, Codex user-scope MCP servers. adoption/templates/codex.config.template.toml [mcp_servers.socraticode] pins the 1.14.0 dist/index.js path, startup_timeout_sec=120, external Qdrant, lmstudio-compatible vLLM/Nemotron embeddings (2048 dimensions, 4096 context, query/passage prefixes), SOCRATICODE_WATCHER=auto, INCLUDE_DOT_FILES=false and SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT=3. Live $HOME/.codex/config.toml matches that engine/environment but omits startup_timeout_sec; the host's untracked .codex/config.toml also contains a project entry and includes 120. git ls-files .codex returned no tracked files, so that host copy is not portable repository configuration.
native_adaptation.lane_rule: Use SocratiCode for conceptual code with an explicit projectPath and no implicit linked projects; check health/index completeness and open the original source before judging. Use bounded original reads/rg for known paths and Serena for symbols/references; choose one context method per artifact. Sources: docs/token-session-handbook.md, Choose one useful context method per artifact and per-tool table; recipes/README.md#local-semantic-code-search. User-scope Codex availability follows docs/decisions/2026-09-25-codex-mcp-scope.md, Decision 1; the routing rationale keeping jCodeMunch project-scoped is in docs/decisions/2026-09-23-claude-user-profile.md, 2026-09-25 addendum.

The fixed scan found invocations in 96/1,010 Ultracode children (9.50%) and 11/301 Codex workers (3.65%), including 2/22 TOKEN LANES children (9.09%); this restricted worker's health/status probe was denied and adds no successful native observation (invoke_by_tool.json; groups/final-verdict-evidence.json#live_probes).
